questions.stem: What is the edge length of the unit cell of a body centred cubic crystal of an element whose atomic radius is 75 pm?
questions.solution:
In BCC, $4r = \sqrt{3}a$
$\therefore a = \frac{4r}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{4 \times 75}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{300}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3} \times 100$ pm = 173.2 pm

questions.stem: The root mean square (rms) speed of $\mathrm{X_2}$ gas is x m/s at a given temperature. When the temperature is doubled, the $\mathrm{X_2}$ molecules dissociated completely into atoms. The root mean square speed of the sample of gas then becomes (in m/s)
questions.solution:
$C_{rms} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$
$T_1 = T$, $T_2 = 2T$
$M_1 = M$, $M_2 = M/2$
$C_1 = X$, $C_2 = ?$
$\frac{C_1}{C_2} = \sqrt{\frac{T_1}{M_1} \times \frac{M_2}{T_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{T}{M} \times \frac{M/2}{2T}} = \frac{1}{2}$
$\therefore \frac{x}{C_2} = \frac{1}{2}$, Hence $\boxed{C_2 = 2x\ \mathrm{m/s}}$

questions.stem: The equivalent conductance of NaCl, HCl and $\mathrm{CH_3COONa}$ at infinite dilution are 126.45, 426.16 and 91 $\mathrm{ohm^{-1}cm^{2}eq^{-1}}$ respectively at $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The equivalent conductance of acetic acid (at infinite dilution) would be

According to Kohlrausch’s law
$\Lambda^{0}_{\mathrm{CH_3COOH}} = \Lambda^{0}_{\mathrm{CH_3COONa}} + \Lambda^{0}_{\mathrm{HCl}} - \Lambda^{0}_{\mathrm{NaCl}}$
$\Lambda^{0}_{\mathrm{CH_3COOH}} = (91 + 426.16 - 126.45)\ \mathrm{ohm^{-1}cm^{2}eq^{-1}}$
$\Lambda^{0}_{\mathrm{CH_3COOH}} = 390.71\ \mathrm{ohm^{-1}cm^{2}eq^{-1}}$

questions.stem:
For the reaction $\mathrm{A + B \rightarrow C}$, we have the following data :
Initial concentration of A (in molarity) | Initial concentration of B (in molarity) | Rate (initial) (Relevant unit)
1 | 10 | 100
1 | 1 | 1
10 | 1 | 10
The order of the reaction with respect to A and B are
questions.solution:
Let us assume $R = K[A]^{x}[B]^{y}$
Where x and y are orders wrt A and B respectively
$\therefore$ We can write from given data
$100 = k(1)^{x}(10)^{y}$ ——— (1)
$1 = k(1)^{x}(1)^{y}$ ——— (2)
$10 = k(10)^{x}(1)^{y}$ ——— (3)
$2 \div 1$ gives
$\frac{1}{100} = \frac{k(1)^{x}(1)^{y}}{k(1)^{x}(10)^{y}}$, $\frac{1}{100} = \left(\frac{1}{10}\right)^{y}$
$\boxed{y = 2}$
$3 \div 1$ gives $\frac{10}{1} = \frac{K(10)^{x}(1)^{y}}{k(1)^{x}(1)^{y}}$
$10 = (10)^{x}$ $\boxed{x = 1}$
So reaction is 2nd order w.r.t B but 1st order w.r.t A.

options.text: Not possible to tell with the given data
First order with respect to both A and B
First order with respect to A and second order with respect to B
Second order with respect to A and first order with respect to B.

questions.stem: If in case of a radio isotope the value of half-life ($T_{1/2}$) and decay constant ($\lambda$) are identical in magnitude, then their value should be
questions.solution:
For a radio decay $T_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{\lambda}$
If $T_{1/2} = \lambda = x$ then $x = \frac{0.693}{x}$
$\Rightarrow x^{2} = 0.693$, $\Rightarrow x = T_{1/2} = \lambda = (0.693)^{1/2}$

questions.stem: Suppose a gaseous mixture of He, Ne, Ar and Kr is treated with photons of the frequency appropriate to ionize Ar. What ion(s) will be present in the mixture ?
questions.solution:
He > Ne > Ar > Kr > Xe > Rn (Order of Ionization energy)

$\therefore C(M) = 1.22 \times 10^{-5}$, Molarity $= \frac{\text{no. of moles}}{\text{vol. of solution(L)}}$
$1.22 \times 10^{-5} = \frac{4/M}{4}$. Hence M = 81967 $\approx$ 82000 g/mol

questions.stem: The correct statement about the magnetic properties of $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}$ and $\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}$ is
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{\overset{+3}{Fe}} = [\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{5}4s^{0}$

questions.stem: The calculated spin-only magnetic moment values in BM for $\mathrm{[FeCl_4]^{-}}$ and $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}}$ are
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{Fe^{+3}} = [\mathrm{Ar}]\ 3d^{5}4s^{0}$
$\mathrm{[FeCl_4]^{-}}$
No pairing as $\mathrm{Cl^{-}}$ is weak field ligand, hence have five unpaired electron (n = 5).
$\therefore \mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ B.M $= \sqrt{5(5+2)}$ B.M = 5.9 B.M
$\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{-3}}$
Pairing takes place as $\mathrm{CN^{-}}$ is strong field ligand but has one unpaired electron (n=1)
$\therefore \mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ B.M $= \sqrt{1(1+2)}$ = 1.732 B.M

questions.stem: The relationship between the pair of compounds shown above are respectively,
‘G’ in the above sequence of reactions is

Case – 1 : An ideal gas of molecular weight M at temperature T.
Case – 2 : Another ideal gas of molecular weight 2M at temperature T/2
Identify the correct statement in context of above two cases.
questions.solution:
As temperature is halved, average KE is halved.
Average speed $(C) \propto \sqrt{\frac{T}{M}}$
In case – I, $(C) \propto \sqrt{\frac{T}{M}}$
In case – II $(C) \propto \sqrt{\frac{T}{2 \times 2M}} = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{T}{M}}$
So average speed is also halved.

options.text: Average kinetic energy and avereage speed will be the same in the two cases
Only average speed is halved in the second case

questions.stem: 63 g of a compound (Mol. Wt. = 126) was dissolved in 500 g distilled water. The density of the resultant solution as 1.126 g/ml. The molarity of the solution is
questions.solution:
Mass of compound (solute) = 63 g
Mole of compound $= \frac{63}{126} = \frac{1}{2}$ mole
Mass of solution = Mass of solute + Mass of solvent
= 63 + 500
= 563 g
Volume of solution = $\frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Density}} = \frac{563}{1.126}$ ml
Molarity $= \frac{\text{mole of compound}}{\text{volume of solution (in L)}}$
$= \frac{\frac{1}{2} \times 1000}{\frac{563}{1.126}}$
$= \frac{1.126 \times 1000}{2 \times 563} = 1$
